answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so a voter’s influence depends on reachable, independently attested mass rather than self-created identities. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance; few walks cross that boundary, limiting the cluster’s aggregate voting weight under normalized walk-based scoring. For example, summit, karst, and opal may be labels, but labels alone confer no trust.
